title: Service Sandbox: Access Controls & Data Safeguards — DPA Annex (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This annex defines minimum contractual and operational controls for vendor access to customer-facing or internal service sandboxes ("test/staging/demo environments") where the vendor may interact with synthetic or production-adjacent data. The intent is to: (a) reduce risk of accidental exposure of personal or sensitive data, (b) provide clear obligations for data handling, and (c) preserve auditability and incident response capabilities.

Scope:
Applies to any Third Party ("Vendor") provisioned with access to a Redwood Inference environment identified in the master services agreement (MSA) as a "Sandbox", "Staging", "Demo", "Test", or similar. This annex supplements the DPA and Security Schedules in the MSA.

Definitions (for the purposes of this annex):
- Sandbox: Any non-production environment used for feature verification, integration testing, demos, or training where Vendor has interactive access.
- Production-Adjacent Data: Data derived from or substantially similar to live production datasets (including masked/anonymized exports).
- Synthetic Data: Fully fabricated data that bears no direct identifier mapping to individuals.
- Masking/Anonymization: Irreversible or reversible techniques applied to data; this annex prefers irreversible transformations unless expressly approved.

High-level obligations (vendor-facing):
1) Permitted Data Types
   - Only synthetic data or production-adjacent data that has been processed to meet the Data Masking Requirements (Section 3) may be used in Sandboxes unless Customer provides explicit written approval for a specific use case.
   - Production PII, payment data, health data, or similar high-risk categories must not be present unless an explicit exception has been granted by the Customer's Security Owner and documented with justification and compensating controls.

2) Provisioning and Access Controls
   - Least privilege: Vendor roles must be scoped to the minimum permissions required for the task.
   - Time-bounded access: Sandbox credentials and IAM roles must have an expiry no later than 30 days unless reapproved.
   - MFA required for vendor operator accounts with interactive access.
   - Vendor access must use a unique identity per individual (no shared accounts).

3) Data Masking and Transformation Requirements
   - All production-adjacent datasets must be transformed prior to sandbox import using irreversible masking techniques where feasible (e.g., synthetic generation, differential privacy, tokenization with one-way hashing + salt stored only in customer-controlled vault).
   - Sensitive fields (PII, auth tokens, internal identifiers that can be reattached to an identity) must be removed or replaced.
   - Data sampling: datasets should be minimized in size and scope consistent with testing needs (e.g., representative slices rather than full exports).

4) Logging, Monitoring, and Telemetry
   - All vendor activity in the sandbox must be logged with user, timestamp, actions performed, and resource identifiers.
   - Logs must be retained for a minimum of 90 days and made available to Customer on request for audit; retention can be longer per Customer policy.
   - Alerting: any access from suspicious IP addresses, abnormal data exfiltration patterns, or bulk downloads must generate an alert to the Customer security contact and the Vendor security contact.

5) Data Egress and Export Controls
   - Exports from the sandbox (downloads, API dumps, snapshots) require documented approval and must use secure channels (SFTP with client certs or HTTPS with mutual TLS).
   - Exports containing production-adjacent data are prohibited without Customer sign-off.

6) Network and Environment Segmentation
   - Sandboxes must be segmented from production networks using network ACLs and/or VPC separation.
   - No direct route from vendor-provisioned sandbox instances to production databases or storage.

7) Secrets and Key Management
   - Vendors must not store production secrets in sandbox environments. If keys are required for testing, use customer-provided ephemeral keys with constrained scope and expiration.

8) Incident Response and Notification
   - Vendor must notify Customer within 24 hours of discovering any suspected or confirmed data exposure impacting Sandbox datasets.
   - Notification must include scope, time window, affected records (estimate), and initial mitigation steps.
   - Vendor must cooperate with Customer-led investigation and provide forensic artifacts (logs, memory snapshots, exported configurations) within agreed SLAs.

9) Audit Rights and Evidence
   - Customer retains the right to audit (or appoint a third party to audit) vendor sandbox controls annually or upon reasonable suspicion.
   - Vendor must provide evidence within 10 business days: provisioning logs, data transformation scripts, export approvals, and sample datasets used for tests (appropriately redacted).

10) Subprocessing and Onboarding
   - Vendor must disclose any subprocessor that will have access to Sandbox environments prior to onboarding them. Subprocessors are subject to the same obligations in this annex.

11) Liability and Remedies
   - Breaches caused by Vendor negligence that result in exposure of Customer personal data from the sandbox will be subject to indemnity provisions in the MSA; parties may negotiate liquidated damages for sandbox-specific incidents.
   - Customer may immediately suspend Vendor access upon reasonable belief of data exposure or systemic noncompliance.

12) Exceptions and Approvals
   - Any deviation from these controls requires written approval from Customer Security and the Customer Business Owner and must be documented with compensating controls and a sunset date.

Operational checklist (to be completed before granting vendor sandbox access):
- [ ] Use case and minimum data required documented (Jira/Confluence link).
- [ ] Data transformation script(s) reviewed and signed off by Customer Security.
- [ ] Access plan with role mapping and expiry dates submitted.
- [ ] VPN/IP allowlist or mTLS certs configured.
- [ ] Logging and retention parameters validated (location, retention period).
- [ ] Export approval workflow configured.
- [ ] Subprocessor disclosure completed.

Acceptance criteria (security team use):
- No raw PII or production credentials present in the sandbox dataset; spot check of 3–5 records.
- Access model enforces unique identities + MFA.
- Audit logs ingest to Customer SIEM and show vendor actions within the last 7 days.
- No network path exists from sandbox to production data stores.

Suggested contract language snippets (pick and adapt):
- "Vendor shall not load, access, or use Production Personal Data in any Sandbox environment unless prior written consent is provided by Customer. All production-adjacent data must be rendered irreversible via the Data Transformation Procedures attached hereto."
- "Vendor shall implement and maintain a least-privilege access model for Sandbox environments, including unique identities for individuals, mandatory MFA, and time-bounded credentials."
- "Vendor will notify Customer within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of any actual or suspected security incident involving Sandbox data and shall cooperate in investigation and remediation."

Evidence items to attach to the agreement (appendices):
- Appendix A: Data Transformation Checklist and Example Scripts
- Appendix B: Sandbox Access Request Template (role map + expiration)
- Appendix C: Logging & SIEM Ingestion Specification
- Appendix D: Subprocessor Disclosure Form

Open questions / items for Legal + Security to finalize:
1) Is the 24-hour notification window acceptable to our higher-risk customers or do we need a 12-hour SLA?
2) Do we allow reversible masking for any analytics vendor workflows (if so, what escrow/dual control is required)?
3) Minimum log retention: 90 days is suggested — needs GTM alignment for enterprise requests.

Notes to negotiators / SEs (working guidance):
- For PLG trials or time-limited demos, favor fully synthetic datasets generated from real schemas; this often reduces negotiation friction.
- Keep any production-adjacent datasets intentionally small and narrowly scoped (e.g., <1k records) and document the business need.
- Use the Operational Checklist as an onboarding gating criterion.
